clue.text: Ecstasy found in room backed dishonest talk about heroin trader

indicators.note: the drug letter is found sitting inside the room letters
backed means the abbreviation for room is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: the hypocritical talk goes round, about, the drug letter

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A dealer is caught with drugs in a room, spinning a dishonest story about heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is someone who buys and sells goods for a living, a synonym for trader.

clue.text: Cuts in central Greece producing blackout

indicators.note: the snips are placed in the middle of the country's central letters
central asks for the letters at the very centre of the country's name

parts.note: the two letters at the centre of the six-letter country name
clips are cuts, as in trims with shears

explanation.surface: Spending cuts in central Greece cause a power blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse blacks out the sun or moon, so it is a natural or astronomical blackout of light.

clue.text: Clubs swindle that puts extra on bill

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
to overcharge is to cheat a customer by asking too much

explanation.surface: Nightclubs run a swindle that adds an extra sum to the customer's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover charge is a fixed fee added to a restaurant or club bill per diner or guest.

clue.text: Often nurses left parcel out

indicators.note: nurses means holds in its arms, so the side letter is held within

parts.note: a lot means often, as in 'I go there a lot'

explanation.surface: Nurses who often work shifts leave someone to hand out a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or distribute portions, which is what parcel out means.

clue.text: Whirlwind to trouble British sailors sucked in

indicators.note: the sailors are drawn into the middle of the other two words, fitting the whirlwind picture

parts.note: taken as written
ado is fuss or bother
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A whirlwind causes trouble for British sailors, who are sucked up into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating column of air, a kind of whirlwind.

clue.text: Penny leaving Greek battle site for shack

indicators.note: the coin's letter leaves, departing from the battle site's name

parts.note: Lepanto, off western Greece, was the site of the 1571 naval battle

explanation.surface: A tourist spends their last penny at a Greek battlefield and sleeps in a shack.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, a rough hut or shack.

clue.text: Survive having to abandon desperate defenders here?

definitions.note: the adjective means desperate, and the question mark points to the literal last trench where defenders make a final stand

parts.note: to last is to keep going, to survive
to ditch is to dump or abandon

explanation.surface: Soldiers wonder whether to survive or abandon their desperate defensive post.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an adjective, but the clue pictures the noun: the final trench where defenders hold out.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt, named after troops fighting from their final trench.

clue.text: Supposedly the greatest length trunk road spans?

indicators.note: the road stretches across, spanning, the measurement letter

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered trunk road, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A trunk road supposedly spans the greatest length of any.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, famously proclaimed himself 'the greatest'.

clue.text: Colossus reportedly becoming tense

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the giant's name is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a colossus is a giant, a titan

explanation.surface: The giant statue becomes taut and stiff, as it is reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten is to make taut, to tense, as in tensing a muscle.

clue.text: The Intersection: gripping stuff penned by novelist

indicators.note: the fastener is enclosed, penned, within the writer's name

parts.note: Doris Lessing, Nobel prize-winning novelist
Velcro is a hook-and-loop fastener whose two sides grip each other

explanation.surface: A gripping novel called The Intersection is written by a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping stuff' suggests an exciting book; it is the fastening material.
explanation.definitionFit: A level crossing is where a railway and road cross on the same level, an intersection.

clue.text: One coming inside stumbles around in shade

indicators.note: the numeral letter comes into the middle of the other word
around means the word for stumbles is turned the other way

parts.note: trips means stumbles

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles around in the shade after coming indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost, the same thing as a spirit of the dead.

clue.text: Sailor, spiteful sort breaking fall, finds step down

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: the nasty person breaks into the middle of the word for fall

parts.note: to die is to fall, as soldiers fall in battle
a cat is a spiteful, catty person

explanation.surface: A sailor, breaking a fall against some nasty fellow, finds a step down.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office, to resign or step down.

clue.text: Classy furniture one's got in now bracket fixed

indicators.note: the numeral letter is got into the rearranged letters
fixed means arranged or rigged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A piece of classy furniture has now had its bracket fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinetwork is fine joinery and furniture made by a skilled cabinetmaker, a superior craft.

clue.text: Flask going into bag as far down as possible

indicators.note: the vacuum flask goes inside the mesh bag

parts.note: a net is a mesh bag, as for vegetables
a Thermos is a vacuum flask

explanation.surface: A flask goes deep into a bag, pushed as far down as it will go.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest, the furthest down of all, a superlative of nether.

clue.text: Runs through — tries to stop Welshman?

indicators.note: the legal word is put in to plug, stop, the middle of the surname

parts.note: Rees is a common Welsh name
a judge hears, or tries, a case

explanation.surface: A runner tries to stop a Welshman in a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like rugby scoring; it is in the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a play or speech, to run through it.

clue.text: Any number seen aboard punt that's leaning

indicators.note: aboard means on the boat, so the letter is inside the word for punt

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a gamble
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Any number of people board a punt that is listing to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests the flat river boat; it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent can mean inclined or having a tendency, a leaning towards something.

clue.text: Lord's ducks perhaps mating animals

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, a batsman out for nought in both innings bags a ..., as might happen at Lord's
second meaning: a couple of animals kept together to breed

explanation.surface: Ducks at a lord's estate may be breeding couples.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; a duck is a score of zero, and two in one match is called a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both two cricket ducks and a breeding couple, a male and female together.

clue.text: Bartholomew maybe after beer bottles

indicators.note: the drink holds, bottles up, the word for after

parts.note: ale is beer
post is Latin for after, as in post-war

explanation.surface: Bartholomew goes looking for bottles of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartholomew was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, an example of an apostle.

clue.text: Arrogant, intoxicated worker appears before news boss

parts.note: high means drunk or drugged
a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand
ED, short for editor, is the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A drunk, arrogant worker turns up before the newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: High-handed means acting overbearingly without regard for others, which is arrogant behaviour.

clue.text: Officer briefly laid on fine blanket

indicators.note: in a down clue, the officer is placed on top of the fine

parts.note: GEN is the short form of general
an eric was a blood-fine in old Irish law, paid by a killer to the victim's kin

explanation.surface: An officer, briefly, lays out a fine blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine blanket' reads as a quality bedcover, but fine is a noun and blanket an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic and blanket both mean covering a whole class, general rather than specific.

clue.text: Composer wanting area green for painter

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the area letter is missing

parts.note: Edward Elgar, English composer
eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: A composer wants an area of green set aside for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance.

clue.text: Caution in favour of conflict between opponents

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: the fighting comes between the two bridge players

parts.note: East and North are opposing players at bridge
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Caution argues in favour of conflict between two opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To forewarn is to caution in advance, to alert someone before danger arrives.

clue.text: Soup label mysterious writer keeps

indicators.note: the author holds, keeps, the label inside

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote mysteries and tales of the macabre
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A mysterious writer keeps the label from a soup tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick French-style soup.

clue.text: Ready with article about Indian city

parts.note: pat means ready, as in having an answer off pat

indicators.note: about means the article is turned around

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is ready with an article about an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Patna is the capital city of Bihar state in India, on the Ganges.

clue.text: Reverse a tutor suffers making valuable discovery

indicators.note: the words suffer damage, so their letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: these three words supply the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tutor suffers a setback while making a valuable discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' tempts a backwards reading; it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure trove is hidden gold or silver found by chance, a valuable find.

clue.text: Dread losing initial musical ability

indicators.note: the word for dread loses its first letter

parts.note: fear means dread

explanation.surface: Someone dreads losing their early musical talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an ear for music means being able to pick out and reproduce tunes well, a musical talent.

clue.text: Dancing bride succeeded causing wreckage

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters jig into a new order

parts.note: the five letters of this word are the ones rearranged
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A dancing bride succeeds in wrecking the reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something destroyed, wreckage.

clue.text: Bananas excellent served with some tea?

parts.note: crack means first-rate, as in crack troops
tea is served from a teapot, a pot of tea

explanation.surface: Bananas are excellent served with a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit with tea; it means mad, the person who is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy; a crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, used adjectivally too.
